curriculum.subject: English Language Activities
curriculum.subStrand: 13.3.1 Yes/ No questions (with can, may, will)
curriculum.outcomeText: realise the use of can, may and will to seek information.

interactions.prompt: Which question asks about an ability?
interactions.feedback: Yes! Can begins a question about ability.
interactions.retryHint: Look for a question that can be answered yes or no.

interactions.prompt: Match each question word to what it asks about.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a question, then the information it seeks.
interactions.feedback: Excellent! Can, may, and will help us seek different information.
interactions.retryHint: Can asks ability, may asks permission, and will asks what is going to happen.

interactions.prompt: You want permission to borrow a crayon. What should you ask?
interactions.feedback: Correct! May asks politely for permission.

interactions.prompt: Sort the sentences into Questions and Statements.
interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a sentence, then its group.
interactions.feedback: Great sorting! Questions seek information; statements give information.
interactions.retryHint: Questions end with a question mark and ask for an answer.

interactions.prompt: You need to know if your friend is coming tomorrow. What do you ask?
interactions.feedback: Well done! Will seeks information about a future action.
interactions.retryHint: Begin the yes-or-no question with Will.

interactions.prompt: Choose the best question starter for each need.

objects.label: ask if Ali knows how to ride

interactions.tapAlternative: Tap a need, then its question starter.
interactions.feedback: Mission complete! You know how can, may, and will seek information.
interactions.retryHint: Match ability with can, permission with may, and future action with will.
